### Observed differences

- The relative order of two groups of activities reversed. In the earlier window, A35, A36 and A41 each ran before A26 and before A27 in about 98–100 of 100 traces; in the later window, A26 and A27 each run before each of A35, A36 and A41 in about 97–99 of 100 traces. All six pairs still co-occur in every trace in both windows, so participation did not change — only their order. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- Positions shifted consistently with this reversal: in the later window A26 sits earlier in the trace (mean position about 0.62 → 0.53) and A27 earlier (0.47 → 0.38), while A35, A36 and A41 each sit later (about 0.41–0.42 → 0.58–0.59). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- Direct successors changed accordingly. In the later window A25 leads almost exclusively to A27 (98 of 100 outgoing transitions, previously split over A35/A36/A41 at about 27–39 each); A26 now leads to A35/A36/A41 (about 30–34 each) instead of almost only to A30 (99 of 100 before); A35, A36 and A41 now lead to A30 (about 31–35 of 100) and practically no longer to A27 (from about 28–37 to under 1). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- Step distances match: A27 now immediately follows A25 (lag 1 in 98 of 100 traces, previously 4–5 steps), and A30 follows A26 only after about 4 steps (91 of 100, previously immediately in 99 of 100). Pairs linking A25 to the group and the group to A27 within five steps nearly vanish (200 → 2 observations each), while A30 now follows A36 within 1–3 steps in 198 of 200 traces. [LAG005, LAG009, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG010, LAG012, LAG011]
- Participation also differs: A06 appears in fewer traces in the later window (about 27 → 12.5 of 100) and its outgoing transitions spread from mostly A16 (86 of 100) across many targets (39 of 100), based on fewer observations (57 → 28); A02 appears in more traces (about 4.5 → 11.5 of 100). [OCC002, OCC001, DIR001, POS001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis of a reordering between the group A35, A36, A41 and the activities A26, A27: in the earlier window the group ran before A26 and A27 (entered from A25 and leading to A27, with A26 leading directly to A30), whereas in the later window A26 and A27 run before the group, A25 leads directly to A27, A26 leads into the group, and the group leads to A30. This rests on direct relational evidence — all six activity pairs flip from one fixed order to the other with about 200 traces per window and unchanged co-occurrence [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006] — and is consistent with the position shifts [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006], the successor changes [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007] and the lag changes [LAG005, LAG009]. With 33 qualifying items against roughly 0.76 expected without change, the evidence set as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is that the two windows sample two coexisting orderings with different frequencies rather than a single modified sequence; several lag items rest on very few observations (2 in the later window) and were not relied upon.

Other differences: A06 is executed in fewer traces (about 27 → 12.5 of 100) and its outgoing transitions spread across more targets, while A02 appears in more traces (about 4.5 → 11.5 of 100); these participation changes are not part of the main hypothesis. [OCC002, OCC001, DIR001, POS001]
